name: Swim in open water
blurb: Pool fitness does not transfer directly: cold, chop, no walls and no black line make open water a distinct skill. Done properly it is one of the best things there is.
gear: A brightly coloured hat and a tow float
A group or a swim buddy, always
steps: Acclimatise gradually to cold water over weeks. Never jump straight into cold water — the shock response is what kills.
Learn to control the initial gasp: enter slowly, submerge to the neck, and wait for your breathing to settle before swimming.
Learn sighting: lift your eyes just clear of the water every six to ten strokes, crocodile-style, without stopping your stroke.
Practise swimming in a straight line by sighting on a fixed high landmark rather than a buoy.
Learn to swim in chop by breathing to the sheltered side and shortening your stroke.
Always swim with others, know the exit points, and get warm quickly afterwards.
tips: Afterdrop is real: you keep cooling after you get out. Dry off and layer up immediately, and skip the hot shower.
Never swim alone in open water, and always be visible to boats with a bright hat and float.
proof: A comfortable one-kilometre open-water swim, sighting accurately, with a safe entry and exit.
